purpose: External research sources that contextualize SEAT outcome scores. Research sources explain what a score exposes a program to. They never change a score, create a gap, or establish compliance status.

sources.name: CrowdStrike 2026 Threat Hunting Report
sources.description: Frontline adversary tradecraft from observed intrusions. Strongest source for whether a program's curriculum and metrics match techniques currently in use.

sources.name: SANS 2026 Security Awareness and Culture Report
sources.description: Practitioner benchmark on staffing, program age, and barriers. Strongest source for resourcing and headcount arguments.
sources.coverageWindow: Eleven years of this report; over 1,700 practitioners worldwide

sources.name: CybSafe Oh, Behave! 2025-2026
sources.description: Population-level attitudes and self-reported behavior. Strongest source for arguing that knowing and doing are separate problems.

sources.name: Fable Security AI Behavior Index, Vol. 1
sources.description: Measured detections across roughly 290,000 employees, broken out by job function. Strongest source for role-based targeting arguments and for AI visibility gaps.

sources.name: Harmonic Security AI Usage Index 2026
sources.description: Observed AI-session minutes across six tools, classified personal versus business. Strongest source for arguing that AI guidance and governance keyed to the enterprise tenant miss where the work actually happens.
sources.coverageWindow: Trailing seven weeks ending April 2026; 1,935,247 classified minutes across a panel of enterprise organizations

sources.name: Verizon 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report (DBIR)
sources.description: Breach-corpus evidence on the human element and shadow AI, from a publisher that sells no remediation against its findings. The anchor source: treat vendor telemetry as corroboration of it. Shadow-AI and insider figures are DLP detection telemetry within the same report.
bestFor: governance keyed to the wrong accounts
sources.coverageWindow: Incident timeframe Nov 1 2024 to Oct 31 2025; 19th annual edition

sources.name: IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026
sources.description: Breach-cost benchmark from organizational interviews. Strongest source for the AI governance gap and for putting a dollar figure on the cost of inaction. Behavioral claims should be read cautiously; its distinctive value is cost benchmarking.
bestFor: shadow AI as a costed incident category
sources.coverageWindow: Breaches March 2025 to February 2026; 3,558 interviews across 602 organizations, 16 countries, 17 industries

sources.name: CISA Insider Threat Mitigation Guide (2026 Edition)
sources.description: Federal best-practice guidance on building insider threat mitigation programs, citing third-party incident studies and surveys on leakage, reporting, grievance, and AI-driven risk. Strongest source for reporting-culture design, training-content checklists, and the case for treating insider risk as more than phishing.
bestFor: AI as a two-directional insider risk
sources.coverageWindow: Program guidance current as of publication; cites underlying studies collected 2005-2025
